answer: One concrete defense is a bond-scaled identity gate. Every new agent entering the orchard must lock a velvet-threaded stake, a deposit sized to its reputation history, before it may transact. Peers who catch a node masquerading as several identities slash that stake and burn it, so each duplicate costs the attacker a fresh bond plus the reputation it had already earned. Spoofing a hundred workers means paying a hundred bonds, which pushes the cost of a sybil swarm past the zenith of any realistic profit, while honest agents pay once and keep their stake working.
